claim: The FIRST structure error — the one audit's dag_shape finding names — is the same error on both runtimes for every dag, independent of JS object key ordering: when several gate values are malformed and the gate keys are integer-like ("10", "9"), shapeErrors and shape_errors enumerate gates in the same order (document/insertion order), so the dag_shape text line and JSON object are byte-identical and the unsorted shape error list agrees.
violation: {"phases":[],"gates":{"10":"x","9":"y"}} audited on both runtimes yields node '[dag_shape] … gates.9 must be an object' and python '[dag_shape] … gates.10 must be an object' (or any other pair of dag_shape lines that differ), while tests/dag-shape.sh k5 and parity.sh shape:audit stay green because their fixtures use non-numeric gate keys.

claim: On a structure-valid dag the structure view IS the dag for every gate key, including the key "__proto__": the post-wave node lint output (errors, warnings, exit) equals the pre-wave a500587 node output and equals python's for a dag whose gate is named __proto__ — the view's rebuilt gates map keeps that gate as an own property, so the criteria-shape rule, the never-referenced warning and audit's gate rules still see it.
violation: {"phases":[{"id":"P","tasks":[{"id":"t"}]}],"gates":{"__proto__":{"criteria":["x"]},"Z":{"criteria":[{"id":"c","cmd":"true"}]}}} lints exit 0 on post-wave node with only 'gate defined but never referenced: Z', while pre-wave node and python both report '[__proto__] criteria entry 0 must be an object with a string cmd (got "x")' plus 'gate defined but never referenced: __proto__' and exit 1 — a gate silently dropped from node's view (and from audit's hollow-gate rules) that k3 cannot see because no existing dag carries the key.

claim: A phase whose id is STRUCTURE-invalid (missing, empty, a number, a boolean) is skipped by EVERY id-keyed rule, checkDetach/_check_detach included: no lint line renders such an id as [undefined], [None], [5] vs [5.0] or [true] vs [True]; the sorted error lists stay byte-identical across runtimes when an invalid-id phase also carries detach fields, and the proof's junk-line detector catches a bracketed undefined/None rendering, not only ': undefined' / '(got undefined' / '= undefined'.
violation: A dag whose phases[0] has no id and carries detached_from/detached_reason/detached_by/detached_at with gate_entry null lints as '[undefined] a detached phase id must be usable as an anchor file name …' on node and '[None] a detached phase id …' on python (likewise id 5.0 → '[5] detach fields are partial …' vs '[5.0] …', id true → '[true]' vs '[True]'), so the two lints' error lists differ on a structure-invalid dag; and echo '[undefined] a detached phase id' passes tests/dag-shape.sh's junk-line grep.

claim: The offending value rendered in the '[G] criteria entry N must be an object with a string cmd (got …)' line — reused verbatim as dag_shape's first error — is byte-identical across runtimes for every JSON value the file can carry: the numbers 1.0, -0.0, 12345678901234567890 and the out-of-range 1e400 (which both parsers accept as an infinity; the contract must either reject it as 'not valid JSON' on both or render it identically), and a string of more than 120 non-BMP characters truncated by code points, not UTF-16 units, on both.
violation: {"phases":[],"gates":{"G":{"criteria":[1.0]}}} audits to '… (got 1) …' on node and '… (got 1.0) …' on python; -0.0 → '(got 0)' vs '(got -0.0)'; 12345678901234567890 → '(got 12345678901234567000)' vs the exact digits; 1e400 → '(got null)' vs '(got Infinity)'; a 130-emoji string → the node slice ends in a broken surrogate half and holds 60 emoji while python's holds 120 — any of these makes the dag_shape finding (and the lint line) differ while k5 and shape:audit, which only use ASCII strings and small ints, stay green.

claim: Nesting depth is file content like any other: for a dag.json whose _meta (or any value) is nested to any depth, neither lint nor audit prints a traceback or a stack trace on either runtime, and the two runtimes agree on the outcome — both accept it as a valid plan with the same output, or both report 'dag.json unreadable: not valid JSON' with exit 1 — because the surrogate scan, the structure walk and the placeholder flatten are depth-safe (iterative or bounded) rather than naively recursive.
violation: {"phases":[],"gates":{},"_meta":[[[…600 deep…]]]} lints '✓ DAG valid' exit 0 on node while python exits 1 with 'RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded' from lint.py _has_surrogate (hb lint and hb audit alike); at depth 5000 node itself dies with a RangeError stack trace from hb-lint.js:35 while python says 'dag.json unreadable: not valid JSON' — a traceback for file content and a cross-runtime exit-status split that k2's fixed-class list never exercises.

claim: The tolerant rest of the audit does not split across runtimes on a STRUCTURE-invalid parked: when parked is [] or {} (truthy in JS, falsy in python), the structure view neutralises it (or both audits treat it the same way), so the non-dag_shape finding set, the error count and the 'parked' list of the audit result are identical on both runtimes — the round-1 F7 split the contract set out to remove does not survive inside audit.
violation: {"phases":[{"id":"P","gate_exit":"G","parked":[],"tasks":[{"id":"t","title":"x"}]}],"gates":{"G":{"criteria":[{"id":"c","cmd":"true"}]}}} audits to errors=1, parked=['P'] (phase skipped as parked) on node and errors=2 with a hollow_gate finding and parked=[] on python (same with parked {}): the two runtimes disagree on how many errors the plan has and on what was audited, while k5 passes because it compares only the dag_shape object.

claim: The reverse pin (tests/dag-shape.sh k4) has teeth at every level the dag-writing verbs write: an undeclared key written into the regate marker, its rearm record or a gate's review is detected — either the schema closes those objects (additionalProperties false, with every key the runtimes write — including review.profile — declared) or the k4 checker treats an unspecified additionalProperties as closed — so a verb that leaks a key below the gate/phase level reddens k4 instead of passing.
violation: Running k4's schema-walk checker over a dag whose gates.G.regate carries "bogus": 1, whose regate.rearm carries "extra": 2 and whose review carries "bogus2": 3 prints 'undeclared: []' and exits 0 (regate, rearm and review declare no additionalProperties, so the checker's default of True skips them); equivalently, a mutant of hb.js / cli.py that writes rg2.rearm.leak = 1 during regate --rearm leaves tests/dag-shape.sh k4 green on both runtimes.
